source_refs.note: Exercise 3.4, Question 8: Exercise 3.4, book page 94: Q1-Q15 (integration by partial fractions); answers book pages 301-302

blocks.explanation:
Pehli nazar mein yeh rational function nahi lagta, kyunke is mein \(e^x\) hai, \(x\) ki powers nahi.
Lekin ghor karein: har jagah \(e^x\) hi \(e^x\) hai. Agar \(t = e^x\) rakh dein to yeh \(t\) ka rational function ban jata hai.
Substitution ke baad denominator \(t^2(t + 1)\) banega, jis mein \(t\) repeated hai, yani Case-II.
Plan: substitution (\(dx\) ko bhi badalna hai), \(t\) mein partial fractions, integral, aur wapas \(x\) mein.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\int \frac{e^x - 1}{e^x(e^x + 1)}\,dx\).
Maloom karna: yeh integral.
Tareeqa: substitution \(t = e^x\) se yeh \(t\) ka rational function banega, phir partial fractions (Case-II). Yeh dikhata hai ke partial fractions sirf seedhe polynomial walon tak mehdood nahi; substitution ke baad bhi kaam aate hain.

\(t = e^x\) rakhein
\[dt = e^x\,dx \;\Rightarrow\; dx = \dfrac{dt}{t}\]
\[\int \dfrac{t - 1}{t(t + 1)}\cdot\dfrac{dt}{t} = \int \dfrac{t - 1}{t^2(t + 1)}\,dt\]
Kyun: \(e^x\) ka derivative \(e^x\) hai, is liye \(dt = e^x\,dx = t\,dx\), yani \(dx = \frac{dt}{t}\). Har \(e^x\) ki jagah \(t\) likha.
Dhyan dein: Sirf \(e^x\) badal kar \(dx\) ko waise hi chhor dena ghalat hai; \(dx\) badalne se hi neeche ek aur \(t\) aaya aur \(t^2\) bana.

\(t\) mein partial fractions
\[\dfrac{t - 1}{t^2(t + 1)} = \dfrac{A}{t} + \dfrac{B}{t^2} + \dfrac{C}{t + 1}\]
\[t - 1 = At(t + 1) + B(t + 1) + Ct^2 \quad (1)\]
Kyun: \(t\) do dafa (power 2) hai, is liye us ke do fractions \(\frac{A}{t}\) aur \(\frac{B}{t^2}\); \(t + 1\) akela hai to \(\frac{C}{t + 1}\). Phir \(t^2(t + 1)\) se multiply.

Constants nikalein
\[t = 0:\ -1 = B\]
\[t = -1:\ -2 = C\]
\[t^2:\ 0 = A + C,\ A = 2\]
Kyun: \(t = 0\) par \(A\) aur \(C\) wale terms zero, \(B(0 + 1) = B\). \(t = -1\) par \(A\) aur \(B\) wale zero, \(C(-1)^2 = C\). \(A\) ke liye koi root nahi bacha, is liye \(t^2\) ka coefficient compare kiya: right side par \(A + C\), left side par 0.

\(t\) mein integral
\[\int \left(\dfrac{2}{t} - \dfrac{1}{t^2} - \dfrac{2}{t + 1}\right)dt\]
\[= 2\ln t + \dfrac{1}{t} - 2\ln(t + 1) + c\]
Kyun: \(-\int t^{-2}\,dt = -\frac{t^{-1}}{-1} = \frac{1}{t}\). \(t = e^x\) hamesha positive hai, is liye modulus ki zaroorat nahi.

Wapas \(x\) mein
\[= 2x + e^{-x} - 2\ln(e^x + 1) + c\]
\[= e^{-x} + 2\ln\left(\dfrac{e^x}{e^x + 1}\right) + c\]
Kyun: \(\ln e^x = x\) aur \(\frac{1}{e^x} = e^{-x}\). Kitab ki shakal ke liye \(2x = 2\ln e^x\) likh kar logs ko jora: \(2\ln e^x - 2\ln(e^x + 1) = 2\ln\frac{e^x}{e^x + 1}\). Dono shakalein ek hi jawab hain.

Tasdeeq
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(2x + e^{-x} - 2\ln(e^x + 1)\right)\]
\[= 2 - e^{-x} - \dfrac{2e^x}{e^x + 1}\]
\[= \dfrac{2}{e^x + 1} - \dfrac{1}{e^x} = \dfrac{e^x - 1}{e^x(e^x + 1)} \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: \(2 - \frac{2e^x}{e^x + 1} = \frac{2e^x + 2 - 2e^x}{e^x + 1} = \frac{2}{e^x + 1}\). Phir common denominator \(e^x(e^x + 1)\) liya: \(\frac{2e^x - (e^x + 1)}{e^x(e^x + 1)} = \frac{e^x - 1}{e^x(e^x + 1)}\). Asal integrand wapas mil gaya.

blocks.text: Kitab ke aakhir mein answers (page 301) mein Exercise 3.4 ke jawab ghalat heading "Exercise 3.6" ke neeche chhape hain. Is sawal ka jawab us block ka item (viii) hai: \(e^{-x} + 2\ln\left(\frac{e^x}{e^x + 1}\right) + c\). Yeh jawab sahi hai. Jis block par "Exercise 3.4" likha hai (page 301) woh kisi aur exercise ke jawab hain, is liye wahan se milane ki koshish na karein.
